turns.t: Doctor, I am Meena, I look after Mr Rao in the daytime. We are here for the check after the eye operation.
Good morning, both of you. Mr Rao, which eye was it? ~
Left. ~
Right, and when was your surgery? ~
Eleven days ago, doctor. He was happy, but now he says vision is a little blurry.
Blurry sometimes.
Is it all the time, or does it come and go?
Morning mostly. Later it is better.
When did the blurriness start, after the operation, or was it there before?
I don't know. Maybe after. Maybe before. I cannot say.
He didn't tell me earlier, doctor. I noticed it only this week.
That's all right, we'll look carefully today. Any pain in the eye?
No pain.
There is no pain, he never complained. ~
Any history I should know about, other medical conditions?
Diabetes, for ten years.
And anyone in the family with eye problems?
My father. Glaucoma. He lost the sight in the end.
Thank you. And how are you managing at home, Mr Rao? Who do you live with?
My son and daughter-in-law. Meena comes in the day. I like to watch cricket on the television.
Good. I'd like to check your vision with the chart now, please read the lowest line you can.
E. F. P.
Good, that's the sixth line, which is good for a recovering eye. ~
Is it normal? ~
Very normal for this stage. Now, I'll use the light microscope to look at the eye. Chin on the rest, Mr Rao, and look straight at me.
Okay. ~
The eye is calm, the cornea is clear, and the new lens is sitting in a good position.
Doctor, then why is it blurry? ~
It's common to have some blur at this stage, as the eye settles. Another possibility is a slight film behind the lens, but that usually comes later. For now, I'm not worried. ~
Good. ~
Any headaches, or eye strain with the television?
No, no headache. TV is fine.
Good. Keep your eye clean, avoid rubbing it, and wear your sunglasses outdoors.
I will make sure he doesn't rub it. ~
If the blurriness gets worse, or the eye becomes painful or red, or you see flashing lights, please come in the same day.
Same day, understood. ~
Otherwise, I'm happy. Thank you both. ~
Thank you, doctor. ~
